newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's ACCC keeps eye on Optus suit - Fels.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's ACCC keeps eye on Optus suit - Fels.

text.p: Anti-monopolies watchdog, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC), said on Friday it would keep an eye on the unfolding legal battle between Optus Communications Pty and Seven Network Ltd over pay television operator, Optus Vision.
"We're monitoring the case," ACCC chairman Alan Fels said.

Seven, which owns 2.0 percent of Optus Vision, claims it has the right to buy the balance of Optus Vision from the other three shareholders - Optus Communications and U.S. West Inc, which hold 46.5 percent each, and Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd which has 5.0 percent.
Seven has alleged a breach of the shareholders' agreement has given it this right.
The court proceeedings regarding the case are scheduled to start on February 24.
Fels told Reuters the ACCC was not harbouring any great concerns about the case at this stage.
"We'll wait and see what happens. We're a fair way off from a situation where Seven's taking over Optus Vision," he said.
